Building model from a laser scan

Project Revit model of a university building, built from a laser scan
Software Revit
Source Course scan data
Context UCL, first year
Model Walls, floors, windows, doors

In first-year coursework at UCL I used Revit to model the exterior of a building from a laser-scan point cloud supplied by the course. The task was set for two mini groups, and I built the model on my own, for both. I placed the levels, walls, floors, windows and doors against the scan.

Car park design for a London site

Project Car park design for the Here East site, London
Software AutoCAD, FME, ArcGIS Pro
Site data OS MasterMap, aerial imagery
Context UCL, first year
Scale 1:705

For a first-year CAD and GIS project I designed a car park on a site next to a building area, using the standard bay and aisle dimensions from the brief. I drew it in AutoCAD, placed it on the site drawing, converted it with FME and mapped it in ArcGIS Pro in 2D and 3D. It includes standard, electric and disabled bays, bike bays, green space, a one-way road and a pedestrian walkway.

Where this started

Working through the redesign showed me how much civil engineering can do, including protecting people in coastal zones. That's why I'm studying it, and why I'm taking Ocean Engineering as a minor. I later gave a Student Society talk on the problems MOSE faces.
